en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga:
The Section on Offenses Entailing Confession (Pācittiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on Exhortation 26.
The Training Rule on Sewing Robes.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Venerable Udāyī was occupied with making robes.
A certain bhikkhunī approached the Venerable Udāyī; having approached, she said this to him:
"It would be good, venerable sir, if the master would sew a robe for me."
Then the Venerable Udāyī, having sewn that bhikkhunī’s robe and made it well-dyed and well-finished, had a decorative design embroidered in the center, folded it up, and set it aside.
Then that bhikkhunī approached the Venerable Udāyī; having approached, she said this to the Venerable Udāyī:
“Venerable sir, where is that robe?”

“Come now, sister, take this robe-cloth as it is folded, lay it aside, and when the community of bhikkhunīs comes for the exhortation, put on this robe-cloth and follow right behind the community of bhikkhunīs.

Then that bhikkhunī took that robe-cloth as it was folded, laid it aside, and when the community of bhikkhunīs came for the exhortation, she put on that robe-cloth and followed right behind the community of bhikkhunīs.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How long will these bhikkhunīs go on being such scoundrels and shameless women, that they actually paint decorative designs on their robes?
The bhikkhunīs asked,
“Whose work is this?”
“It was for Master Udāyī.
“Even for those shameless scoundrels who have been expelled, such a thing would not look well; how much less so for Master Udāyī!
Then those bhikkhunīs reported this matter to the bhikkhus.
Those bhikkhus who were of few desires … [as before] … complained, grumbled, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the venerable Udāyī sew a robe for a bhikkhunī? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, Udāyī, that you are sewing a robe for a bhikkhunī?”
“It is true, Blessed One.
“Are your kinsmen, Udāyī, unrelated to you?
“They are unrelated, Blessed One.”
“A man unrelated to her, foolish man, does not know whether [a robe] is suitable or unsuitable, pleasing or unpleasing.
How, foolish man, can you sew a robe for a nun who is unrelated to you?
This, foolish man, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence... [and so forth].”
And thus, monks, you should recite this training rule:
“Whosoever, however, a monk should sew a robe for an unrelated nun, or have it sewn, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Whosoever, however:
Whoever is such a person … [as described] … is called a “bhikkhu” … this is the meaning intended by the term “bhikkhu” in this context.
"Non-relative" means not connected by blood on the mother's side or the father's side, up to the seventh generation of ancestors.
"Bhikkhunī" means...
One who is fully ordained in both Saṅghas.
"Robe" means any one of the six kinds of robes.
"Should sew herself" means:
she sews it herself; at each stitch, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
"Should have sewn" means: [she causes another to sew it].
If she instructs another, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If, having been instructed once, she sews even many [robes], there is an offense of expiation.
If she sews a robe or has it sewn for a woman who is not related to her, perceiving her as one who is not related, there is an offense of expiation.
If he sews a robe or has one sewn for a woman who is not related to him, while being in doubt [about her relationship], there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If he sews a robe or has one sewn for a woman who is not related to him, perceiving her to be related, there is an offense of expiation.
If he sews a robe or has one sewn for a woman who is ordained on only one side [of the Sangha], there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she is a relative and he perceives her as not being a relative, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If she is a relative and he is uncertain, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If she is a relative and he perceives her as a relative, there is no offense.
There is no offense if she sews or causes to be sewn another requisite, excluding a robe, for a relative.
for a trainee nun,
for a novice nun,
for one who is insane,
"For one who is a first-time offender.
The sixth training rule concerning the sewing of robes is concluded.
